edits.old: About 3.2–3.3 M lidar units were installed in 2025 (3.21 M in §B1; ≈3.32 M per NE Times in §B7.1), at roughly 1.3–1.6 units per car (§F2). Lidar cars are therefore probably only a few percent of China's car fleet in 2026 [E]: 2025's installations correspond to $3.21\ {\rm M}/1.6\approx2.0$ M to $3.32\ {\rm M}/1.3\approx2.6$ M lidar cars. Adding 2024 (1.53 M units, §B1) and 2026 (985k units in Q1, §B1, and an assumed 4–5 M for the whole year) gives $1.53+3.21+4\approx8.7$ M to $1.53+3.32+5\approx9.9$ M units installed in 2024–2026, i.e. $8.7/1.6\approx5.5$ M to $9.9/1.3\approx7.6$ M lidar cars. Installations before 2024, not quantified here, add to this, so the stock is roughly 6–8 M lidar cars by end-2026. That is about 2% ($7\ {\rm M}/350\ {\rm M}$) of a Chinese car fleet assumed at ≈350 M [U].
edits.new: About 3.2–3.3 M lidar units were installed in 2025 (3.21 M in §B1; ≈3.32 M per NE Times in §B7.1). GGAI (高工智能汽车研究院), which counts cars as well as units, puts 2025 at 3.25 M units on 2.56 M new cars, i.e. $324.84/256.28\approx1.27$ units per car, below the 1.3–1.6 assumed in §F2 [MR/E]. Earlier years add little: GGAI counts 0.11 M lidar cars in 2022 and 0.44 M in 2023 (0.13 M and 0.57 M units), about 4,000 in 2021 and 1.37 M in 2024 [MR/E], so about $0.004+0.112+0.440+1.374+2.563\approx4.5$ M lidar cars were on China's roads at end-2025 [E]. Adding 2026 (985k units in Q1, §B1, and an assumed 4–5 M for the whole year) at 1.27 units per car gives $4.5+4/1.27\approx7.6$ M to $4.5+5/1.27\approx8.4$ M lidar cars by end-2026 [E]. That is about 2% ($7.6/371\approx2.0\%$ to $8.4/371\approx2.3\%$) of the 371 M automobiles registered in China at 30 June 2026, a count that includes trucks and buses [P, Ministry of Public Security], so lidar cars remain only a few percent of the fleet [E].
